newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator wants peacekeeping costs out of defense.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator wants peacekeeping costs out of defense.

text.p: U.S. defense funding has hit "rock bottom" and an agency other than the Pentagon should pay for peacekeeping efforts, the new chairman of the Senate Appropriations Committee said Wednesday.

"We're down to a very low ebb of expenditure in defense compared to our national economy and our national budget," Sen. Ted Stevens, R-Alaska, said. "It's reached rock bottom as far as I'm concerned," he added.
Stevens did not specify which peacekeeping efforts should be paid for by other agencies. The biggest U.S. peacekeeping operation now is in Bosnia.
Asked which other domestic programs he would cut if defense spending was not reduced, Stevens replied: "I don't expect to cut ... I expect to have rather a level budget."
While changes in the defense budget will be needed, Stevens said he would not participate in any substantial cuts to defense spending.
"I do want to try to eliminate some of the expenditures that have been placed within the defense account in the past that I think really are peacekeeping costs," Stevens said.
"They are not costs of maintaining the defense of this country and we ought to find some different way how to allocate funds to meet those costs," he said.
"Currently we are reducing the effectiveness of our military because we are spending so much money for these peacekeeping costs," Stevens said.
While he did not disagree with peacekeeping activities, they should be paid out of non-defense budgets, Stevens said.
The current level of defense spending should at the very least be maintained and if more money was available it could be used for national missile defense, he said.
